channel.title: The Honolulu Star-Advertiser - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Honolulu Star-Advertiser (staradvertiser.com)

item.title: Jesse Jackson, civil rights leader who sought presidency, dies at 84
item.description: The Rev. Jesse Jackson, whose impassioned oratory and populist vision of a “rainbow coalition” of the poor and forgotten made him the nation’s most influential Black figure in the years between the civil rights crusades of the Rev. Martin Luther King Jr. and the election of Barack Obama, died today. He was 84.

item.title: Warner Bros gives Paramount one week to beat Netflix deal
item.description: Warner Bros Discovery today rejected Paramount Skydance’s latest $30-a-share hostile bid, but gave the Hollywood studio seven days to come up with a “best and final” offer for the owner of HBO Max and the “Harry Potter” franchise.

item.title: Strong winds, high surf buffeting Hawaiian islands prompt advisories
item.description: Gusty tradewinds and high surf are buffeting the Hawaiian islands today as Hawaiian Electric officials monitor weather conditions for potential power shutoffs for Maui County.

item.title: Bayer proposes $7.25B plan to settle Roundup cancer cases
item.description: Bayer said today its Monsanto unit had filed a proposed U.S. class settlement totalling as much as $7.25 billion aimed at resolving all current and future claims that its Roundup weedkiller caused cancer.

item.title: Colbert: CBS blocked interview with Democrat candidate over FCC fears
item.description: DALLAS >> CBS “Late Show” host Stephen Colbert said the network blocked an interview with James Talarico, who is running for the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate in Texas, preemptively caving to pressure from the FCC.

item.title: Groups sue Trump administration to block history purge in parks
item.description: BOSTON >> Groups representing park conservationists, historians and scientists filed a lawsuit today seeking to prevent President Donald Trump’s administration from scrubbing information from parks and monuments, after exhibits and signs touching on topics like slavery and climate change were removed.

item.title: U.S. kills 11 in boat strikes in Pacific and Caribbean
item.description: U.S. forces blew up three boats overnight, killing 11 men in strikes in both the eastern Pacific Ocean and Caribbean Sea, the military announced today. The strikes raised the death toll in the U.S. campaign against people it accuses of drug smuggling at sea to at least 144.

item.title: Dollar edges higher against peers; yen strengthens
item.description: NEW YORK >> The U.S. dollar edged higher against major currencies today as geopolitical tensions from the ongoing U.S.-Iran nuclear talks unleashed more market uncertainty and a risk-off mood among investors.

item.title: Glove found near Nancy Guthrie’s home fails to produce DNA match
item.description: TUCSON, Arizona >> One of the most promising leads yet in the investigation into the abduction of Nancy Guthrie proved a disappointment today when DNA from a glove found near her Arizona home failed to score a match in a national database of genetic profiles.

item.title: Felony abuse, escape suspect arrested at police station
item.description: Tiofilusi Tongamoa, who escaped custody on Jan. 17 after allegedly assaulting his wife inside their Aiea residence in front of their children, who were under 14, was arrested at 3 p.m. Monday and taken into custody at the main police station at 801 S. Beretania St.
